items.title: Lathoa: Math app where AI deliberately makes mistakes for kids to catch
items.summary: A math learning app for ages 10–14 where an AI robot solves problems with one intentional error per solution; kids find and explain the mistake to build critical thinking and AI literacy skills.
items.endUser: Kids aged 10–14 and their parents or teachers building AI literacy and math error-detection skills
items.costStructure: Free tier (3 cases/day); paid yearly subscriptions (Learner, Parent, Family tiers) with founding-member discount for first 50 families
items.howItWorks: Errol the robot generates step-by-step math solutions with one deliberate error. Each case passes through arithmetic verification and a second independent model solve before reaching the child. Kids highlight the wrong step, explain the error in their own words, and earn detective ranks.
items.inputNeeded: Kid selects a math case and reads Errol's step-by-step solution
items.outputGiven: Error detection practice, explanation writing, detective rank progression, replayable case history
workflow: Kid opens a case
Errol shows step-by-step solution with one error
Kid identifies wrong step
Kid writes explanation of the error
Errol reveals correct solution
Kid earns rank points
useCases: Homework-table practice for spotting AI hallucinations
Classroom supplement for critical thinking math skills
Sibling sharing on one device with Family plan
items.hardwareRequirements: Runs in any browser, iOS, and Android
items.subscriptionsRequired: Free tier available; paid plans (Learner, Parent, Family) for unlimited cases, replay, and parent dashboard
items.author: thanouil1411

items.title: Corral – Kill every process an AI agent spawns, guaranteed
items.summary: Corral runs a shell command with a wall-clock limit and verifies that no descendant process survives when the command exits. It uses a cgroup v2 group (enforced mode) or proc-tree scanning (fallback mode) to catch daemons, background jobs, and processes that ignore SIGTERM.
items.endUser: AI coding agent authors and CI pipeline maintainers who need guaranteed cleanup of shell commands they did not write
items.costStructure: Free (MIT licensed)
items.howItWorks: Corral starts the command in a new session so signals to the command's process group cannot reach corral itself. It becomes a child subreaper so orphaned processes are reparented to it. In enforced mode the command runs in a dedicated cgroup v2 group; one write to cgroup.kill stops the entire tree. In fallback mode corral scans /proc via pidfds, signals remaining processes, and reaps them until none remain. The run ends when the command exits, not when pipes close.
items.inputNeeded: A shell command to run, plus optional flags for wall time, grace period, memory limit, PID limit, output limit, and JSON audit path
items.outputGiven: Exit code of the command (or corral-specific codes 120, 121, 122, 124, 125, 126, 127, 128+N) and optional JSON audit record with timestamps, PIDs, and termination reason
workflow: Install corral binary (prebuilt or from source)
Run `corral --wall 30s -- your-command`
Corral starts command in new session as subreaper
Command executes; corral monitors time and resource limits
On exit or timeout, corral kills entire process tree via cgroup or /proc scan
Corral verifies no descendants remain, then returns exit code
useCases: Prevent leftover daemons from AI agent `bash` tool calls
Ensure CI jobs release ports and file locks after timeout
Bound memory and PID usage of untrusted build scripts
items.hardwareRequirements: Linux 5.11+ (5.14+ for enforced mode), x86-64 glibc 2.36+
items.integrations: systemd-run (for cgroup delegation in enforced mode)
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed
items.author: CG144

items.title: Offrun – manage every coding agent from one workspace
items.summary: A free Mac app that runs Claude Code, Codex, AGY, and Grok Build side by side in isolated git worktrees, with built-in code review by a second agent, automatic account switching on usage limits, project memory, preview, and on-device dictation.
items.modelUsed: Claude Code (user-selected model), Codex, AGY (Antigravity CLI), Grok Build
items.endUser: Solo devs and small teams running multiple coding agents who want parallel workflows, automated code review, and seamless usage-limit handling
items.costStructure: Free (Offrun); bring your own agent subscriptions
items.howItWorks: Offrun launches the CLIs of your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, AGY, Grok Build) on your Mac, each in its own git worktree so parallel agents never edit the same files. It stores project-wide conventions and per-agent goals as plain files in your repo, renders diffs and previews beside the chat, transcribes dictation locally, and when one agent account hits its usage limit it moves the conversation to another connected account.
items.inputNeeded: Project folder, connected agent account logins, tasks or prompts (text or dictation)
items.outputGiven: Code changes in isolated git worktrees, diffs with line numbers, rendered previews (markdown, tables, images, PDFs), reviewer findings in chat, transcribed dictation text
workflow: Install Offrun on Apple Silicon Mac (macOS 14+)
Connect coding agent accounts in Settings
Start an agent, pick a project, give it a task
Run multiple agents in parallel (each gets own git worktree)
Optionally assign a reviewer agent to read diffs
Review changes and merge on your schedule
useCases: Run a refactor and a bug fix simultaneously in the same repo
Have a second agent review code before you see it
Switch to a second agent account when the first hits usage limits
Dictate prompts on-device without uploading audio
items.hardwareRequirements: Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or newer) running macOS 14 Sonoma or later
items.integrations: Git (worktrees), Anthropic (Claude Code), OpenAI (Codex), Google (AGY), xAI (Grok Build)
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed for Offrun; requires existing agent subscriptions (Claude Code, Codex, AGY, Grok Build)
items.author: arunbhatia

items.title: ldraw-nova: Open-source AI LEGO model generator using LDraw language
items.summary: An open-source dockerized web app that lets AI agents generate buildable LEGO models in LDraw format, with 3D viewing, VR support, and Blender export.
items.endUser: LEGO enthusiasts and developers experimenting with agentic AI for physical CAD design
items.costStructure: Free (open source); requires API keys for OpenAI, Claude, or OpenRouter; TypeSafe API key optional for improved search
items.howItWorks: The agent reads LDraw documentation and examples, plans a model structure, then iteratively writes Python generator scripts that output LDraw source code. It uses headless rendering to inspect and adjust the model until satisfied. The final output is an .mpd file viewable in LEGO CAD tools, 3D web viewers, VR on Meta Quest 3, and exportable to Blender as glTF.
items.inputNeeded: Natural language prompt describing the desired LEGO model
items.outputGiven: LDraw source code (.mpd/.ldr), 3D web viewer, 3D player, VR interactive (Meta Quest 3), rendered images, Blender-editable glTF (.glb), chat history, agent thinking process
workflow: Clone ldraw-nova and ldraw-nova-docker repos
Build Docker image (~5GB disk)
Start app via docker compose
Open https://localhost:8443 or http://localhost:8765
Enter model prompt in web UI
Agent generates plan, writes generator script, produces LDraw model
View result in 3D viewer, VR, or export to Blender
useCases: Generate custom LEGO models from text descriptions
Prototype LEGO designs for physical building
Experiment with agentic AI for CAD geometry tasks
items.hardwareRequirements: Docker with ~5GB disk space; Meta Quest 3 for VR features
items.integrations: OpenAI API, Claude API, OpenRouter API, TypeSafe API, Meta Quest 3
items.subscriptionsRequired: Paid API plan for OpenAI, Claude, or OpenRouter; TypeSafe API key optional
items.author: antelocnova

items.title: Weave Router 2.0: Open-source model router for coding agents at Astra-level performance
items.summary: Weave Router 2.0 plugs into coding agents like Claude Code and intelligently routes tasks across an ensemble of LLMs, matching GPT-6 Astra performance at ~52% cost and 2.2x speed on Terminal Bench 4.0.
items.modelUsed: Weave Router 2.0 (custom routing model); routes between models including Astra and Deepseek v4 Flash
items.endUser: Developers using Claude Code or Codex who want to reduce LLM costs and latency
items.costStructure: Free (open source); hosted version available at weaveos.com/router
items.howItWorks: The router uses a hidden Markov model to trace session state, then a classifier maps sessions to buckets of similar models. It calculates cache-eviction impact to decide when switching models is worth the cost, shrinking the 10^100 routing search space dramatically.
items.inputNeeded: A coding agent session running in Claude Code or Codex
items.outputGiven: Per-turn model selection that routes each agent call to the optimal LLM
workflow: Install Weave Router
Connect to Claude Code or Codex
Run coding agent session
Router selects optimal model per turn
Task completes at lower cost and faster
useCases: Tricky debugging or complex system design tasks routed to Astra
Simple frontend updates routed to Deepseek v4 Flash
Any coding agent session needing cost and latency optimization
items.integrations: Claude Code, Codex
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed
items.author: adchurch

items.title: Computer vision tool evaluates deadlift form with SAM 3.1, ViTPose+, Gemma 4 26B
items.summary: A side-on video analyzer that counts reps, times each pull, and classifies back position as straight or rounded with per-frame probability, using three open models via VLM Run Gateway.
items.modelUsed: SAM 3.1, ViTPose+ Large, Gemma 4 26B (gemma-4-26b-a4b-it) via VLM Run Gateway
items.endUser: Lifters and coaches who want frame-level deadlift form data from side-on video
items.costStructure: Free tool; VLM Run Gateway API usage costs apply (run.json records per-model cost)
items.howItWorks: SAM 3.1 tracks the near plate to measure bar height in meters and count reps via hysteresis. ViTPose+ Large computes the shoulder–hip–knee angle as a backup rep counter and hip-hinge visual. Every frame, cropped to the lifter, is sent to Gemma 4 26B as a structured choice question returning {"straight": p, "rounded": 1-p}; the mean P(rounded) over the first pull (floor to knee) decides the rep verdict.
items.inputNeeded: Side-on deadlift video clips with whole lifter and near plate in frame, placed in data/input/
items.outputGiven: Timestamped output folder with overlay video (live probability panel), timeline.png (bar height, hip angle, P(rounded) per rep), reps.json, reads.json, summary.txt, run.json (config, provenance, cost)
workflow: Get VLM Run API key at app.vlm.run/sign-in
Add key to .env at repo root
Create and activate conda env from environment.yml
Place side-on clips in data/input/
Run python main.py (or with flags for single clip, credit, etc.)
Find results in data/output/<timestamp>/
useCases: Quantify back rounding probability per rep to track form changes over time
Cross-check rep counts from bar path vs. hip hinge angle for reliability
items.hardwareRequirements: ffmpeg with libplacebo for HDR tone-mapping; on macOS, moltenvk Vulkan driver (conda install -c conda-forge moltenvk)
items.integrations: VLM Run Gateway API
items.subscriptionsRequired: VLM Run Gateway API key required (sign in at app.vlm.run/sign-in)
items.author: dr_blueberry

items.title: Breadcrumb: Local Mac recorder with MCP tools for AI
items.summary: Breadcrumb records screen, meetings, and AI transcripts on a Mac, encrypts everything locally, and exposes 30+ MCP tools so an AI assistant can search memory and act on it. It runs entirely locally, is free, and gives developers full observability of their AI‑driven workflow.
items.endUser: Solo developers using AI coding assistants on Mac who want a private, searchable memory of all their work
items.costStructure: Free (open beta, no account required)
items.howItWorks: Breadcrumb continuously captures screen OCR, meeting audio with diarization, and AI tool transcripts, storing them in an encrypted SQLite database. A local Ollama instance runs Gemma 3 4B to classify and name entries. The indexed memory is exposed via 30+ Model‑Context‑Protocol (MCP) tools, allowing any compatible AI (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode) to query context and execute actions such as bug triage or ticket creation.
items.inputNeeded: Mac with 16 GB+ M‑series chip; install Breadcrumb and grant screen‑recording and microphone permissions
items.outputGiven: Encrypted local timeline of screen text, meeting transcripts, AI tool logs; 30+ MCP tools for AI to search, summarize, and act on that memory
workflow: Download and install Breadcrumb on Mac
Grant screen recording and microphone permissions
Start recording screen, meetings, AI transcripts
Indexes data locally, encrypts with SQLCipher
AI accesses memory via 30+ MCP tools
AI completes tasks like bug review, tickets
useCases: Review a Zoom meeting, extract every discussed bug, and auto‑create JIRA tickets with screenshots
Trace a production bug back to the first AI action that caused it and add a rule to prevent recurrence
items.hardwareRequirements: 16 GB+ M‑series Mac
items.integrations: JIRA, Slack, Zoom, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed
items.author: jv22222

items.title: Token compression CLI cuts Codex API costs 30% with fine-tuned Qwen
items.summary: Yolanda and Spencer built a free CLI that wraps Codex with a proxy and a fine-tuned Qwen model to strip verbose tool-call outputs before they re-enter the context, preserving KV cache and agent trajectory while reducing input tokens by ~30%.
items.endUser: Developers using OpenAI Codex who hit high API bills on context-heavy coding tasks
items.costStructure: Free
items.howItWorks: A local proxy intercepts Codex tool-call results, feeds them to a fine-tuned Qwen model trained to compress output while preserving file-retrieval accuracy and agent trajectory, then returns the compressed results to Codex so the KV cache stays intact and fewer tokens are billed.
items.inputNeeded: Codex tool-call outputs / agent trajectory
items.outputGiven: Compressed tool-call results with preserved trajectory and file-retrieval accuracy
workflow: Install CLI via curl script
Run Codex normally (compression on by default)
Proxy intercepts tool-call results
Qwen compresses results preserving trajectory
Compressed results return to Codex
Token usage and cost drop ~30%
useCases: Cut Codex API spend on large codebase navigation
Reduce tokens for multi-file refactoring tasks
items.integrations: Codex (OpenAI); SDK and API keys offered for product integration
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed
items.author: yolandac

items.title: Parrot – Open-Source Mac Meeting Recorder with Live AI Co-Pilot
items.summary: Parrot records any audio your Mac hears, transcribes and diarizes locally with Whisper or Parakeet, and runs a live assistant that suggests answers from your own documents during the call. Post-call it writes a structured report with action items and coaching, all on-device unless you opt into cloud APIs.
items.modelUsed: Whisper (local), Parakeet v3 (local), Ollama (local LLMs), optional: Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Groq, Deepgram, TypeSafe, LM Studio
items.endUser: Solo professionals, founders, sales reps, and recruiters who run frequent video/voice calls on macOS and want live, document-grounded assistance without a meeting bot
toolsUsed: Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex (MCP-style integration)
items.howItWorks: Parrot auto-detects when a call starts and records system + mic audio with echo cancellation. Transcription and speaker diarization run on-device using Whisper or Parakeet. Your PDF/text/markdown documents are chunked and embedded locally via Apple's language models. During the call, the assistant (Ollama local LLM or your cloud key) retrieves relevant passages and shows answer cards in real time. After the call, the same pipeline generates a summary, action items, objections, talk-balance metrics, and coaching notes, each linked to the transcript line. Everything stays on the Mac unless you enable cloud transcription or a cloud LLM.
items.inputNeeded: Mac audio (system + microphone), optional documents (PDF, .txt, .md), optional calendar access, optional API keys for cloud providers
items.outputGiven: Live answer cards during calls, speaker-labeled transcript, post-call report (summary, action items, objections, talk balance, coaching), searchable meeting history, exports to Obsidian/Reminders/webhook
workflow: Install Parrot (signed, notarized) on macOS 14+ Apple Silicon
Optionally connect calendar and add reference documents
Choose profile (Sales discovery, Interview, etc.) or create custom
Start recording (⌘R) – Parrot auto-detects call apps
Live assistant shows document-grounded answer cards
Stop recording (⌘-.) – report generates instantly
Ask Parrot about past meetings (⌘K) or export notes/actions
useCases: Sales discovery: live objection handling from pricing FAQ, post-call coaching on talk ratio and missed buying signals
Candidate interviews: live red-flag detection, structured scorecard report with evidence timestamps
Customer success calls: instant recall of prior commitments, auto-draft follow-up email with action items
items.hardwareRequirements: macOS 14+, Apple Silicon (M-series); model downloads require several GB disk space
items.integrations: Google Meet, Zoom, Teams, any audio-playing app; Calendar (auto-profile selection); Obsidian, Reminders, Zapier/Make webhooks; Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed. Cloud features use your own API keys/accounts (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Groq, Deepgram, TypeSafe).
items.author: turantekin

items.title: Perspica – semantic diff tool for reviewing AI-generated code changes
items.summary: Perspica parses code diffs with tree-sitter to group changes by intent, filter mechanical noise, and surface hidden issues like broken call sites. Optional LLM analysis (via Claude Code, API keys, or local Ollama models) adds risk ratings, summaries, and maps changes to your original prompts when using Claude Code or Codex.
items.modelUsed: Optional: claude-opus-5-5 (default), claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-4-5 via Claude Code or Anthropic API; gpt-4o via OpenAI API; gemma4:12b, qwen3-coder:30b via Ollama
items.endUser: Developers reviewing large AI-generated PRs from Claude Code or Codex, and teams wanting semantic diff review without sending code off-machine
items.costStructure: Free (core); optional LLM analysis uses your existing Claude Code subscription, API key costs, or local hardware for Ollama
items.howItWorks: Perspica runs a local tree-sitter parse on both sides of a diff, fingerprints symbols ignoring formatting, matches items across versions, classifies each change (rename, signature change, logic change, move, extraction), builds a cross-file call graph, and renders a reading order from entry points down. An optional LLM pass groups classified changes by intent, rates risk, and checks each group against your Claude Code/Codex session prompts to label changes as 'asked' or 'agent's call'.
items.inputNeeded: A git repository with changes (branch, PR, staged, commit range, or two files)
items.outputGiven: Semantic diff view in terminal, JSON, or local web viewer showing changes grouped by intent, mechanical noise collapsed, reading order, broken call sites, unused code, and optional LLM risk summaries with prompt mapping
workflow: Install binary or build with cargo
Run perspica in a git repo
Review semantic diff in terminal or --web viewer
Optional: run -s for LLM analysis with chosen provider
Navigate changes by intent, reading order, or file
useCases: Review a large PR authored by Claude Code to see which changes you requested vs agent decisions
Quickly understand a teammate's AI-generated PR without line-by-line diff fatigue
Catch broken call sites and unused code after a refactor before merging
items.hardwareRequirements: Runs on macOS, Linux, Windows; Ollama local models need ~16 GB RAM for gemma4:12b, ~32 GB for qwen3-coder:30b
items.integrations: Git, GitHub CLI (gh), Claude Code, Codex, Ollama
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed for core features; LLM analysis uses existing Claude Code login, API keys, or local Ollama
items.author: sshah03

items.title: Omnesis – Self-hosted private knowledge layer for AI agents
items.summary: Omnesis is a self-hosted context layer that syncs your email, messages, health, files, calendar, finances, photos, and more into a local encrypted graph, then exposes it to any tool-using agent (ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, etc.) or its own private companion app — all running on your hardware.
items.modelUsed: User-configurable local models for embedding, OCR, audio transcription, and the Omnesis agent (runs on own hardware or zero-retention cloud providers)
items.endUser: Individuals who want private, full-life AI recall across email, chat, health, finance, photos, and documents on hardware they control
toolsUsed: OAuth integrations for each data source
items.costStructure: Free (self-hosted); optional cloud inference pay-per-use
items.howItWorks: Omnesis connects to opted-in sources via OAuth, continuously syncs data in the background, runs local embedding, OCR, and transcription to build a unified people-and-document graph, and serves that graph to external agents through tool calls or to its own read-only companion agent. Cloud inference is opt-in and zero-retention; everything else stays on your machine.
items.inputNeeded: OAuth credentials for chosen sources (Gmail, WhatsApp, iMessage, Apple Notes, Notion, Calendar, Health, Drive, Contacts, Strava, Granola, bank, Coinbase, browser, Screen Time, call logs, voicemail, location); local machine for indexing and model inference
items.outputGiven: Local searchable graph with citations, agent tool endpoints for external LLMs, private companion chat with grounded answers
workflow: Install Omnesis CLI on your machine
Add sources via one-click OAuth (e.g., omnesis sources add gmail)
Background sync builds encrypted local graph
Connect external agents via tool use or open companion app
Query your digital life with full citations
useCases: Trace a contract from email to WhatsApp to signed PDF in Drive with timeline citations
Correlate health metrics, calendar events, and location visits for a given week
Extract receipts from photographed screenshots and match to bank transactions
items.hardwareRequirements: Machine you control with storage for full personal index; sufficient RAM/GPU for local embedding, OCR, transcription, and agent models if running fully local
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed (self-hosted); optional cloud inference pay-as-you-go
items.author: adrienconrath

items.title: Answer me with HTML — agent skill that answers hard questions with a readable one-page HTML
items.summary: An agent skill that lets AI agents answer complex questions by generating a single, self-contained HTML page with diagrams, tables, and visual explanations instead of walls of text. The model writes only a Markdown draft (~1/7 the tokens) while a bundled CLI handles layout, theming, and diagram rendering, delivering pages ~3x faster and ~27% cheaper than asking for HTML directly.
items.modelUsed: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (benchmarked); works with any agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, etc.)
items.endUser: Developers and technical users who want AI agents to explain complex concepts with visual, readable HTML pages instead of long text responses
items.costStructure: Free (no subscription; optional ElevenLabs API key for video narration)
items.howItWorks: The agent writes a short Markdown draft with structured components (sequence diagrams, flow charts, tables, timelines, etc.) and passes it to the CLI. The CLI computes panel placement and diagram coordinates with dagre, applies a theme (blueprint or shadcn), validates the draft against ASD-STE100 writing rules, and outputs a single HTML file with embedded CSS/JS that works offline. Errors are returned with line numbers for the agent to fix in one retry.
items.inputNeeded: A natural-language question or request for explanation (e.g., 'Explain the TCP three-way handshake', 'Map out how modules fit together', 'make a 3b1b-style video on the TCP handshake')
items.outputGiven: A single self-contained HTML file saved to ~/.answer-me-with-html/pages/ with diagrams, tables, timelines, or explainer video player; optionally an MP4 video file with --mp4 flag
workflow: Install skill via npx skills add
Ask agent a complex question
Agent writes Markdown draft
CLI renders draft to HTML page
Page opens in browser and saves to disk
useCases: Explain TCP three-way handshake with sequence diagram, state diagram, and flag table
Visualize repo module organization with folder tree and call graph
Compare Redis vs Memcached with comparison table and verdict
Create 3Blue1Brown-style explainer videos with synced narration and animations
items.hardwareRequirements: Node.js 20+; for MP4 export: Chrome, ffmpeg, Node.js 22+
items.integrations: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and 70+ other agents via vercel-labs/skills; ElevenLabs API for video narration
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed
items.author: QingYunA

items.title: oil-ui: AI UI Design Methodology Skill for Agents
items.summary: A Skill that gives AI agents a structured design methodology to create polished, differentiated UI designs with a built-in comparison page for reviewing directions.
items.endUser: Developers and designers using AI agents to produce production-ready UI designs
items.costStructure: Free (open source) / Paid Pro version 69 CNY one-time
items.howItWorks: Install the Skill via npx, then give an agent a design task. The agent follows a multi-step methodology: categorize the product, define tone scales, start from concrete references, design distinct first-screen skeletons, verify differentiation across directions, polish memorable moments, and present options in a side-by-side comparison page for selection.
items.inputNeeded: Design task description, optional brand assets, screenshots, or existing project
items.outputGiven: Multiple design directions as previewable HTML pages with a comparison page for selection
workflow: Install Skill via npx skills add oil-oil/oil-ui
Give agent a design task with any reference materials
Agent applies methodology to produce distinct design directions
Review directions in the built-in comparison page
Select a direction for the agent to refine further
useCases: Exploring multiple visual directions for a new product landing page
Polishing an existing interface against its own design system
Recreating a page from a screenshot with responsive layouts
items.hardwareRequirements: Runs on macOS (tested); Windows and Linux untested
items.integrations: draw-ui for image-first design, oil-motion for scroll-driven animations
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed for open source version; Pro is 69 CNY one-time purchase
items.author: oil-oil

items.title: universal-modder – AI agent that mods almost any PC game
items.summary: A plugin and CLI that give any AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, etc.) a complete skill set to discover, reverse‑engineer, generate assets with fal, test in‑game, record a showcase video and publish a mod for virtually any single‑player PC title you own.
items.modelUsed: fal models (GPT Image 2, Nano Banana 2, FLUX, Trellis 2, ElevenLabs) via fal MCP; any host LLM such as Claude Code (Anthropic), Codex (OpenAI), Gemini (Google) can drive the agent
items.endUser: Indie modders and hobbyist developers who own PC games and want AI‑assisted creation of gameplay mods, new assets, or cross‑game mashups
items.costStructure: Free core tooling; fal cloud asset generation requires a paid fal API key (pay‑per‑generation), local ComfyUI path is free
items.howItWorks: The agent installs the universal‑modder plugin, runs `um scan` to fingerprint the game engine and locate a safe modding route, then follows the mod‑any‑game skill loop: recon → reverse‑engineer code → generate sprites/3D/audio via the fal MCP (or local ComfyUI) → verify the mod in the running game → record a video → package the mod and write a field note back to the shared knowledge base.
items.inputNeeded: Path to a locally installed game you own; optional fal API key for cloud asset generation
items.outputGiven: A functional game mod (code, assets, packaging) plus an optional showcase video and a field‑note entry added to the community knowledge base
workflow: Install universal‑modder plugin for your AI agent
Run `um scan` to detect engine and modding route
Agent executes mod‑any‑game loop: recon, reverse‑engineer, generate assets via fal
Test the mod in the live game and record a showcase video
Package the mod and optionally submit a field note PR
useCases: Add a homing missile launcher and tactical nuke to Terraria (tModLoader)
Create a new civilization with a unique 3D‑rendered unit for Age of Empires II DE
Run real Minecraft inside GTA V story mode with cross‑game physics interaction
items.hardwareRequirements: Windows (native or WSL), macOS, or Linux with Python 3.10+, ffmpeg, Blender for 3D→sprite rendering; GPU recommended for fal cloud generation but not required for local ComfyUI
items.integrations: fal MCP server, local ComfyUI, Steam/Epic/Xbox install detection, mod loaders (tModLoader, Fabric, ScriptHookV, BepInEx, Harmony, UE4SS, REFramework, SKSE)
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription for core; fal API key needed for cloud asset generation (pay‑per‑use)
items.author: rehan-remade

items.title: EasyRead: Local-first PDF paper translator with side-by-side view, AI chat, and literature management
items.summary: EasyRead is a desktop app that translates English research papers into formatted Chinese while preserving formulas, tables, and layout. It runs locally, lets you choose any LLM (Claude Code, OpenAI, Ollama, etc.), and adds side-by-side comparison, highlights, notes, AI Q&A, and a searchable literature library with offline HTML export.
items.endUser: Researchers, graduate students, and academics who read English papers and want formatted Chinese translations with AI-assisted reading and personal library management
items.howItWorks: An Electron wrapper launches a local Python service (port 8765) that serves a web UI. You import PDFs via drag-and-drop, arXiv ID, DOI, or URL; the backend translates page-by-page in the background using your selected model (Claude Code, Codex, cloud APIs, or local Ollama/LM Studio). Formulas render via KaTeX, tables as three-line tables, references kept intact. A side panel shows original pages synced to scroll position. You can highlight in four colors, add notes, ask an AI chat panel (multi-model, streaming) about selected text or colored highlights, and edit translations inline. All data — PDF, page images, translations, notes, chats — stays in per-paper folders on disk; a settings option migrates the library to any cloud-synced folder. Export produces a single offline HTML file with everything embedded.
items.inputNeeded: Local PDF files, arXiv IDs, DOIs, paper titles, or paper URLs (OpenReview, ACL, NeurIPS, bioRxiv, PMC, journal pages)
items.outputGiven: Translated paper with formatted Chinese text, KaTeX formulas, three-line tables, side-by-side original text toggle, synced original-page view, highlights, notes, AI chat responses, literature library with categories/progress/citations, exportable single-file offline HTML
workflow: Download and run installer (Windows .exe, macOS .dmg, Linux .AppImage) or `pip install git+https://github.com/Edwardxlai/easyread`
Open app → Settings → Models → add and select a translation model
Drag a PDF into the window or paste an arXiv ID/DOI/URL to import
Wait for background page-by-page translation; read translated pages as they appear
Use toolbar on paragraph click: highlight, note, ask AI; open side-by-side or original-page view
Manage papers in library sidebar; export offline HTML via right-click or CLI
useCases: Translate a 30-page arXiv preprint into formatted Chinese while keeping formulas and tables intact
Ask the AI panel "What's the connection between the formulas I highlighted in red?" and get a streaming answer
Build a personal literature library with custom categories, reading status, and GB/T 7714/APA/BibTeX citations
Send a colleague a single HTML file containing the translated paper, your highlights, notes, and original pages
items.hardwareRequirements: Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon), or Linux; for local Ollama models: GPU with VRAM for chosen model (qwen3.5:9b needs ~8 GB, 4b variant for smaller GPUs)
items.integrations: Obsidian, Notion (via Markdown export); cloud sync via user's own synced folder (iCloud, OneDrive, Dropbox, etc.); GitHub Pages (via `easyread demo` export)
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed for local Ollama/LM Studio models; Claude Code requires Anthropic subscription; cloud APIs require respective API keys (some have free tiers)
items.author: Edwardxlai

items.title: yomiyasu: Agent Skill for Refining AI-Generated Japanese into Natural Japanese
items.summary: yomiyasu is an open-source Agent Skill that rewrites AI-generated Japanese text into natural, readable Japanese by fixing unnatural metaphors, ambiguous subject-predicate relationships, and excessive formatting while preserving original meaning.
items.builtBy: 大賀 愛一郎 (oga_aiichiro) @ ALGO ARTIS
items.endUser: Japanese technical writers, developers writing documentation, and teams producing specs, PR descriptions, or internal reports with AI assistance
items.costStructure: Free (MIT License)
items.howItWorks: The skill applies seven transformation principles to input text: verifying subject-predicate-modifier relationships, preserving sentence function and style, removing anthropomorphism, converting metaphors to plain language, checking preamble and contrast roles, avoiding added information, and adjusting sentence length and punctuation. It includes two Python linting tools for static analysis and diff checking.
items.inputNeeded: AI-generated Japanese text (technical articles, specifications, PR descriptions, reports)
items.outputGiven: Refined Japanese text with natural phrasing, clear subject-predicate structure, and appropriate formatting
workflow: Install via npx skills add nanaism/yomiyasu or npx openskills install nanaism/yomiyasu
Load the skill in your AI coding environment (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex)
Paste draft text and prompt: 'この文章を読みやすくして' or specify domain (tech/business/essay)
Review the refined output
Optionally run yomiyasu_lint.py or yomiyasu_diff.py for quality checks
useCases: Polishing AI-written technical blog posts and code explanations
Cleaning up AI-generated specification documents and PR descriptions
Refining internal reports and design documents drafted with AI
items.hardwareRequirements: Runs on any system with Python 3; no GPU or external dependencies required
items.integrations: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Claude.ai Web (via custom skill ZIP)
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed
items.author: nanaism

items.title: CopilotKit/OpenDots: Template for AI coworkers that work across chat, calls, and Slack
items.summary: OpenDots is a self-hosted TypeScript template for building an agent workspace where named "Dots" act as persistent AI coworkers — they research, write, browse, run code, and hand off work through human-in-the-loop review, all while moving between text chat, voice calls, and Slack threads.
items.modelUsed: OpenAI-compatible model provider via TanStack AI (configured in .env)
items.endUser: Developers and small teams building custom AI agent workspaces with persistent coworkers
items.costStructure: Free (MIT licensed, self-hosted)
items.howItWorks: The web app (React + CopilotKit SDK) streams AG-UI events to a CopilotKit runtime that coordinates specialist compute agents via TanStack AI. Each Dot gets an isolated OpenBot computer (browser, shell, files) with per-Dot permissions. Conversations persist in CopilotKit Intelligence Threads; human-in-the-loop cards pause tool calls for approval. Slack mentions route through Channels SDK into the same Threads. Voice calls use a WebRTC speech bridge that delegates compute to a separate agent while sharing context.
items.inputNeeded: Node.js 24, npm, .env with model provider credentials, optional Slack app credentials, speech provider credentials, OpenBot browser/service containers
items.outputGiven: Running local agent workspace at http://127.0.0.1:5173 with Spaces, Pages, Specialist Dots, chat, voice calls, Slack integration, and persistent per-Dot computers
workflow: Clone repo and install dependencies
Copy .env.example to .env and add model provider keys
Run npm run dev to start the web app
Create Spaces and configure Specialist Dots with roles and tools
Optionally connect Slack, speech, and OpenBot computer services
Chat with Dots, approve drafts, start calls, or mention them in Slack
useCases: Researcher Dot browses web, saves notes to a Page, Writer Dot turns findings into a draft, you approve via human-in-the-loop card
Team mentions a Dot in Slack to delegate a task, continues the thread in the web app with full context and computer access
Start a voice call with a Dot while it runs a long browser task in the background, minimize call to keep chatting
items.hardwareRequirements: Docker for OpenBot browser/service containers; Node.js 24 runtime
items.integrations: Slack (via Channels SDK), OpenAI-compatible model APIs, WebRTC speech providers, OpenBot computer service
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed for the template; external model, speech, and Slack services may require their own paid plans
items.author: CopilotKit

items.title: feder-cr/dots: Open-source AI agent with undetectable Firefox browser
items.summary: An AI agent that ships its own patched Firefox engine to avoid detection — real fingerprints, human-like input events, persistent profiles, and proxy-aware locale matching. Swap any OpenRouter model with one flag.
items.modelUsed: Any model on OpenRouter (configurable via --model flag)
items.endUser: Developers building web automation agents that hit anti-bot walls, researchers needing undetectable browser sessions, anyone automating sites that block headless browsers
items.costStructure: Free (MIT licensed); OpenRouter model usage is pay-per-token
items.howItWorks: Dots bundles a C++-patched Firefox that presents a consistent, seedable fingerprint (screen, fonts, GPU, timezone, language) with no WebDriver flags or automation globals. Pointer movements and keystrokes are synthesized as trusted events. Profiles persist logins and cookies across runs. Proxies automatically align timezone and language. The agent connects to any OpenRouter model and exposes a live split view at localhost:8765.
items.inputNeeded: OpenRouter API key, natural-language task prompt, optional --model, --seed, --proxy, --profile-dir
items.outputGiven: Completed web task results, live browser view at http://127.0.0.1:8765 (conversation left, browser right)
workflow: Install uv (Python package manager)
Run uvx --from git+https://github.com/feder-cr/dots dots --openrouter-key <key>
Open http://127.0.0.1:8765 in browser
Type task in left panel
Watch agent drive real Firefox on right
useCases: Check flight prices across date ranges without airline blocks
Scrape sites that fingerprint and block headless Chrome
Automate login-required workflows with persistent sessions
Run MCP tools (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) with stealth browser via invisible_playwright_mcp
items.hardwareRequirements: Runs Firefox; typical desktop RAM/CPU sufficient
items.integrations: OpenRouter (models), MCP clients (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI), Playwright
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription for dots; OpenRouter requires API credits
items.author: feder-cr

items.title: VibeWise: Claude Code plugin that teaches you to build while AI writes code
items.summary: VibeWise is a Claude Code plugin that puts learning first by guiding you through design checkpoints before AI implements code, so you understand the architecture and tradeoffs while building.
items.endUser: Aspiring engineers, junior developers, and experienced engineers exploring unfamiliar stacks who want to learn software design while building
items.costStructure: Free (MIT license); requires Claude Code access
items.howItWorks: The plugin adds structured checkpoints (Build, Design, Implementation) into Claude Code sessions. At each checkpoint, Claude asks you to reason through the problem in plain English, proposes a design, and only writes code after you confirm. It stores your learning notes and project map in a local .vibe-wise directory, adapts teaching depth to your experience level (Beginner/Intermediate/Advanced), and explains every implementation with tests and diagrams.
items.inputNeeded: Project requirements or existing codebase; answers to design checkpoints in plain English
items.outputGiven: Implemented code with explanations, passing tests, and learning notes stored in .vibe-wise/ directory
workflow: Add VibeWise marketplace in Claude Code
Install vibe-wise plugin
Enable auto-update and restart Claude Code
Run setup and choose experience level
Ask Claude to build a feature
Work through Build, Design, and Implementation checkpoints
useCases: Learning to design a notes app with folder relationships and deletion logic
Exploring an unfamiliar repository with guided system mapping
Practicing software architecture decisions with AI-assisted tradeoff analysis
items.integrations: Claude Code
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed for plugin; requires Claude Code access
items.author: nykooi1

items.title: Television – open-source GUI for any agent harness
items.summary: Television gives you and your agent a shared visual workspace for creating, organizing, and revisiting artifacts — cards, interactive views, or web pages — across persistent channels. It works with any agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) and runs locally via a CLI/server plus a macOS client (browser fallback).
items.modelUsed: Whatever inference provider your agent harness already uses
items.endUser: Solo devs and small teams using agent harnesses who want a persistent, organized visual workspace for agent-generated artifacts
toolsUsed: Agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, Pi, OpenCode, etc.)
items.costStructure: Free (open source)
items.howItWorks: A lightweight CLI and server install on the machine running your agent harness (Linux or macOS). The server communicates with a macOS client app (or browser) that displays artifacts. You equip your agent with 'skills' — reusable instructions — so it can create and update artifacts on your Television screen. Artifacts persist in channels and remain fully editable through continued agent conversation.
items.inputNeeded: An agent harness that can run commands and write files; skills definitions for artifact types
items.outputGiven: Persistent, themeable visual artifacts (cards, interactive views, web pages) organized in channels, editable via continued agent chat
workflow: Install Television CLI and server on agent machine
Launch macOS client app (or open browser version)
Add skills to your agent harness configuration
Chat with your agent normally
Agent creates/updates artifacts on Television screen
Organize artifacts into channels and revisit anytime
useCases: Pin status cards and checklists from coding agents for quick reference
Build and iterate on small web apps or dashboards with agent assistance
Organize research, specs, and prototypes across persistent project channels
items.hardwareRequirements: Linux or macOS for CLI/server; macOS for native client (browser fallback available)
items.integrations: Any agent harness that can execute commands and write files
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed
items.author: stlhood

items.title: Pi Codex Connectors: Use Codex Plugins Inside Pi
items.summary: A Pi extension that exposes all Codex (ChatGPT) connectors and direct web search to any Pi model through a unified three-tool interface, letting you call hundreds of external tools without leaving Pi.
items.endUser: Pi users who want to access Codex connectors and web search from their local models
items.costStructure: Free (open source npm package; requires ChatGPT account with Codex/connectors access)
items.howItWorks: The extension starts a local Codex app-server on first use, which owns your ChatGPT login and connector credentials. It builds a catalog of available connectors and their tools via three unified tools (codex_connectors, codex_connector_schema, codex_connector_call) instead of exposing hundreds of individual schemas. Tools execute through the app-server's MCP interface without running a Codex model turn. Direct web search uses Codex's alpha/search endpoint with your access token, offering cached, indexed, or live retrieval modes.
items.inputNeeded: Codex login with connected connectors; Pi with Node.js 22.19+; user queries for connectors or web search
items.outputGiven: Connector tool results or web search results (with citations) inserted into the Pi model's context
workflow: Install extension via 'pi install npm:@wileai/pi-codex-connector'
Run 'codex login' to authenticate with ChatGPT account
Start Pi and run '/codex-connectors' to discover available tools
Call 'codex_connector_call' with tool name and JSON arguments
Or use 'codex_web_search' with query parameters for web search
useCases: Call GitHub, Linear, Notion, or other connected Codex tools from a local Pi model
Search the web with cached, indexed, or live retrieval modes without leaving Pi
Use hundreds of Codex connectors through a unified three-tool interface
items.hardwareRequirements: Runs on any machine with Node.js 22.19+ and Pi installed
items.integrations: Codex connectors (GitHub, Linear, Notion, etc.), Codex web search endpoint
items.subscriptionsRequired: ChatGPT account with Codex/connectors access (free tier available)
items.author: alexandroskyr

items.title: DASP: Durable Actor Session Protocol for persistent agent sessions
items.summary: A language-agnostic protocol specification for durable actor sessions that survive disconnections, enabling multiple clients to share session history and resume work from saved outcomes.
items.builtBy: Author of Jido (Elixir Actor & Agent SDK)
items.endUser: Builder teams implementing durable, multi-client agent servers and clients
items.costStructure: Free
items.howItWorks: Clients connect to a DASP server to open or resume actor sessions. Commands are submitted with stable IDs; the server saves admission receipts and final outcomes separately. Ordered updates are retained after disconnect, allowing clients to reconnect and read missed events from their last applied cursor. Multiple clients (web, CLI, services) can share one session with identical history.
items.inputNeeded: Protocol-compliant client implementation and a DASP server (Elixir reference implementation planned)
items.outputGiven: Persistent actor sessions with command receipts, saved outcomes, ordered update history, and connection recovery
workflow: Open or resume a session via session.open
Submit commands with stable IDs
Receive admission receipt from server
Read saved outcome (completed, failed, cancelled, uncertain)
On reconnect, read updates after last applied cursor
Share session across multiple clients with same history
useCases: Long-running agent tasks that survive network interruptions
Multi-device collaboration on a single agent session
CLI and web UI sharing the same agent workflow state
items.hardwareRequirements: Runs on any hardware supporting Elixir/TypeScript runtime
items.integrations: Jido Elixir ecosystem (planned server), custom transports and storage
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed
items.author: mikehostetler

items.title: SCM: Local AI search for every photo and video frame on macOS
items.summary: SCM (Screen Memories) is a macOS app that lets you search your entire photo and video library using natural language, with zero cloud uploads. It runs vision, OCR, and speech models locally on your Mac to find scenes, text, and spoken words inside videos.
items.endUser: Mac users with large personal photo/video libraries who want private, offline semantic search without uploading to cloud services
items.costStructure: Free
items.howItWorks: You point SCM at folders of photos and videos. It watches those folders, extracts embeddings for each image and video frame using a local CLIP or SigLIP model, runs Tesseract OCR on every frame, and transcribes audio with Whisper. Search queries are embedded and matched against the local index; results show thumbnails with timecodes for video scenes, highlighted OCR matches, or exact dialogue snippets. An optional llama.cpp sidecar can chat over the extracted evidence with citations.
items.inputNeeded: Folders of photos and videos on macOS (watched folders auto-import)
items.outputGiven: Semantic search results across files, video scenes with timecodes, OCR text matches with highlighted boxes, exact dialogue transcripts with seekable snippets, and optional cited LLM answers over extracted evidence
workflow: Install via Homebrew or build from source
Grant folder access and select libraries to watch
Wait for initial model downloads (~435 MB vision, ~150 MB Whisper, ~17 MB OCR packs)
App indexes files: embeds images, segments videos, runs OCR, transcribes audio
Search by natural language, OCR text, or exact dialogue; filter by saved tabs
Open results to jump to exact video moment or view matched image
useCases: Find a video clip by describing a scene ("dog jumping in snow") and jump straight to that moment
Locate a screenshot containing a specific error message or email address via OCR search
Search spoken words in recorded meetings or lectures without cloud transcription
Ask a local LLM questions about your media library with citations to source frames
items.hardwareRequirements: Apple Silicon Mac, macOS 12+; 8 GB RAM minimum for default models, more for larger LLMs
items.integrations: None (fully local, no cloud services)
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed
items.author: allenleee

items.title: Google Maps Scraper MCP Server
items.summary: A remote MCP server that lets AI agents search Google Maps for up to 20 businesses and receive structured listing data — addresses, contacts, ratings, review counts — via a single authenticated HTTP endpoint.
items.modelUsed: Any MCP-compatible AI agent (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, etc.)
items.endUser: Developers building AI agents that need live local business data for prospecting, market analysis, or CRM enrichment
items.costStructure: Paid API entitlement required for live data; test credentials with simulated fixtures available free
items.howItWorks: The server exposes a single MCP tool, search_google_maps, over stateless Streamable HTTP at https://gmapscrawl.com/api/mcp. Clients authenticate with a Bearer API key, send a keyword and location, and receive up to 20 businesses as structured JSON. The MCP protocol handles initialization and capability negotiation automatically.
items.inputNeeded: Search keyword and location (e.g., "coffee shops in Seattle")
items.outputGiven: Structured JSON with up to 20 businesses including names, addresses, phone numbers, websites, ratings, review counts, and categories
workflow: Create API key at gmapscrawl.com
Add server to .mcp.json with Bearer auth header
Set GMSCRAPER_API_KEY in client environment
Launch MCP-compatible client (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)
Ask agent to search businesses by keyword and location
Receive structured JSON results in the conversation
useCases: Build targeted prospect lists for sales outreach
Compare ratings and categories across local competitors
Enrich CRM records with current business contact details
items.hardwareRequirements: Runs on any machine with an MCP-compatible client; no local GPU required
items.integrations: Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, any MCP client supporting remote HTTP with custom headers
items.subscriptionsRequired: API entitlement (cloud service) required; standard Online subscription does not include MCP access
items.author: qwikhost

items.title: Janus – Go binary that runs GGUF models via Vulkan on AMD/Intel/Nvidia
items.summary: Janus is a single Go binary that runs local GGUF models via llama.cpp with Vulkan acceleration on AMD, Intel, and Nvidia GPUs, exposing an OpenAI-compatible API with hot-swap model support and zero external dependencies.
items.modelUsed: llama.cpp (Vulkan backend) running any GGUF model
items.endUser: Developers who want a local OpenAI-compatible LLM server without Python, Docker, or Ollama
items.costStructure: Free (MIT license)
items.howItWorks: Janus compiles to a standalone executable that loads llama.cpp through a Vulkan backend (or CPU fallback). It reads GGUF models from a local folder, auto-detects chat templates from model metadata, and serves an OpenAI-compatible REST API on localhost:8990. Models can be swapped at runtime via a dedicated endpoint without restarting the server.
items.inputNeeded: A GGUF model file placed in the models/ folder and a .env configuration file
items.outputGiven: OpenAI-compatible API at http://127.0.0.1:8990/v1 with /v1/chat/completions, /v1/models, streaming, and model management endpoints
workflow: Clone repository and run build script
Download a GGUF model into models/ folder
Configure .env with model path and backend
Run janus executable
Call API from any OpenAI-compatible client
useCases: Run local LLMs in Cursor or Cline via OpenAI-compatible base URL
Hot-swap between different quantized models for testing
Script local inference with curl or PowerShell without Python environment
items.hardwareRequirements: Vulkan-capable GPU recommended (AMD/Intel/Nvidia); CPU fallback supported; 2–8 GB disk per model plus ~50 MB for binary
items.integrations: Cursor, Cline, any OpenAI-compatible client
items.subscriptionsRequired: No subscription needed
items.author: Maverick617

items.title: Premortem – AI agents that red-team your startup idea
items.summary: Six specialized AI agents simultaneously critique a startup idea across market, tech, competition, unit economics and more, while a seventh synthesizer compiles their findings into a premortem memo in under 90 seconds.
items.endUser: Founders and early-stage teams validating or stress-testing startup ideas before building
items.howItWorks: User pastes a startup idea. Six AI agents run in parallel, each attacking a different dimension — market, tech, competition, unit economics, and others. A seventh synthesizer agent aggregates their outputs into a single premortem memo. The full cycle averages under 90 seconds.
items.inputNeeded: A text description of the startup idea
items.outputGiven: A premortem memo synthesizing critiques from six analytical perspectives
workflow: Paste startup idea into the input box
Six agents analyze in parallel across different dimensions
Synthesizer agent compiles findings into a memo
Receive the premortem report
useCases: Validate a startup concept before committing resources
Identify blind spots in business model or unit economics
Stress-test competitive positioning and market assumptions
